doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Befriending bassist Hayes Alvis
summary: Through Jimmy Ryan's he met Hayes Alvis, who played with Ellington and the Mills Blue Rhythm Band, became close friends and later his executor.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Gee I never heard that name.

Yeah. He was a bass player who played with Duke Ellington, he played in the Mills Blue Rhythm Band, he was the straw boss there in fact, and he had played with Benny Carter and with many, many. And he came originally from Chicago. He was a drummer in the Chicago Defender Band at one time. And so I met him and I knew about him. And he lived — at the time that I really got to know him was when I took the orthodontic course at Columbia University. Because then I lived with my wife at 175th Street in Washington Heights, which wasn’t too far from Edgecomb and 159th Street, where Hayes Alvis had a five room apartment on the ground floor. And we got to be very good friends. Eventually he made me the executor of his will and I felt that was a very — bit of an honor. He would bring musicians out. And I remember once he brought Louie Bacon, the trumpeter. And immediately when I had a little music room and we sat in the music room and I put on “In the House Blues” with Bessie Smith. And Louie Bacon said, “Who’s that on trumpet?” I said, “Well the books say it’s you.” He said, “Oh no,” he said, “that’s not me.” He said, “You put on New Orleans ‘Hop Scop Blues’ and you’ll see, because I was an admirer of Louis Armstrong and you’ll see that I play a little bit like that.
